newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish slightly higher, quiet day.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish slightly higher, quiet day.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Wednesday after a slow day due to the abbreviated U.S. session.
"The market was very apathetic with few active people," said a trader at an Argentine brokerage house.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 121.10, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 advanced 1/8 to 85-6/8.
Traders expected a slow session through the rest of the week with stable prices because of the absence of U.S. players as U.S. markets are closed for Thursday's holiday.
Traders said Argentine Brady bonds were supported by firm U.S. Treasuries.
However, most peso-denominated issues fell. The peso Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 slipped 15 centavos to 93.45.
"The market needed a cleaning out, so a small decline was foreseen considering this month's gains," said an analyst.
Peso bonds have outperformed dollar ones recently.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.45 percent from 5.60 percent.
